identity.description: Nonparametric POPULATION survival curve — the survival floor. Covariate-free: consumes only the (duration, event) pair, no feature matrix at all. Every covariate survival model (Cox, AFT, RSF) is compared against this baseline; if a model cannot beat the KM curve's summary, its covariates are earning nothing.

axes.note: interpretabilityClass 'Coefficients' is the least-wrong of the 4-value axis: the fitted state IS the fully-inspectable step-function curve (parameters-as-the-model). Flagged as an axes-vocabulary tension for reconciliation. learningType 'Supervised' because it fits the labeled (duration,event) target — the intercept-only survival model — despite consuming zero covariates.

consumes.note: covariate-FREE: consumes only the (duration, event) pair; no feature columns used (the population baseline)

portTypeProposals.name: target:duration-event
portTypeProposals.carries: the bare (duration, event-indicator) column pair with zero covariate columns
portTypeProposals.rationale: KM is the proof-case that a survival component can be target-only. Typing its input as features:tabular would tell the composer a feature matrix is consumed when it is ignored — a dishonest composition contract. A distinct target-only port also lets the wiring UI show 'baseline comparator' components as feature-independent.
portTypeProposals.adapterFallback: features:tabular -> target:duration-event, strategy: project-target-columns, lossless (drops only covariates, which KM ignores by construction)

emits.note: ONE population curve S(t) with Greenwood confidence bands — per-model granularity, NOT per-row (every subject gets the same curve; that is the point of a baseline)

learnsVsFixed.note: learns the curve from data, but its role in compositions is COMPARATOR, not scorer: the baseline every covariate survival model is measured against. Cheap to refit per population/segment.

alpha.note: CI level for the Greenwood bands — a reporting knob, not a fit hyperparameter; KM has essentially no searchable hyperparameters (that honesty is itself catalog signal)

invariances.why: no covariates enter the estimator — there is nothing to scale; the product-limit formula uses only risk-set counts at ranked event times

the estimator depends only on the ORDER of event/censoring times (risk sets at ranked event times); a monotone transform of duration relabels the time axis but leaves every step's height identical — and covariate transforms are vacuously irrelevant
a missing duration or event indicator makes the row's risk-set membership undefined — such rows must be rejected, not imputed (imputing a TARGET fabricates evidence)
vacuous — no covariate pathway exists; stratified KM (one curve per group) is a composition-level group-by, not native categorical handling
fully nonparametric: no proportional-hazards form, no AFT time-rescaling, no assumed lifetime distribution — the empirical product-limit is assumption-free given independent censoring
defined at any event count; as events thin the steps get coarse and the Greenwood bands widen honestly — degradation is visible, not silent
the curve is undefined beyond the last observed time; if the last observation is censored the tail never reaches 0 and is unidentified — no parametric form exists to extend it

featureStats.why: THE commit-survival stat: the fraction right-censored is what makes any survival treatment necessary vs a fixed-window classifier — and KM is the first thing censored data buys
the effective sample size of the product-limit estimator is the number of EVENTS — each step exists only at an event time, so few events means a coarse, wide-banded curve
the maximum observed duration bounds where S(t) is estimable at all — the curve simply stops there, which decides whether the business's horizon of interest is even answerable

modelMetrics.why: the single-number population summary the curve exists to give — the time at which S(t) crosses 0.5, with Greenwood CI; undefined when the curve never reaches 0.5 (report RMST instead)

0.5 BY CONSTRUCTION for a covariate-free curve (every subject gets the same prediction, zero discrimination) — its role here is the FLOOR: the number every covariate model's C-index must beat to justify its features

edgeCases.behavior: S(t)=1 everywhere — computable but vacuous; no survival information exists
median undefined when S never crosses 0.5; tail beyond last event unidentified
edgeCases.note: report restricted-mean survival time (RMST) up to the last event time instead of the median

edgeCases.condition: very few subjects at risk at late times
edgeCases.behavior: late steps are huge and Greenwood bands explode — the tail looks dramatic but is noise
edgeCases.note: truncate reporting at a minimum-risk-set threshold

driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: (duration,event) columns extracted from the input; NO feature matrix consumed. predict maps to survival_function_ / median_survival_time_; per-row scoring is a broadcast of the single population curve

placementClaims.why: no covariate pathway; a missing duration/event is a reject-input (target imputation fabricates evidence), never an impute step
no covariates to transform, and the estimator is rank-based in time
scaleSensitive is false by mechanism — there are no covariates
no categorical covariates exist to encode; stratification is a composition concern, not preprocessing
